text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Solid growth in the September quarter has been fuelled by strong business investment and a resurgent manufacturing sector, but soft consumption spending and a strong build-up of stocks raise the possibility of weaker growth in the future. Page 1.

Although the leadership of John Howard looks secure, the race between Peter Reith and Peter Costello as leadership aspirants is one of the most fascinating internal struggles of the new Government. While they share very similar histories, they are using different styles in their fight for the next leadership position. Page 1.

The ACTU opened its submission to the national wage case yesterday by arguing for large increases in minimum award wages to ensure low-paid workers share in Australia's economic growth. According to the ACTU, Australia's economy is now strong enough to spport a redistribution towards wages and away from profits. Page 3.

A judgement handed down by the New South Wales Industrial Relations Commission has awarded a retrenched senior manager from David Jones compensation for lost income up to retirement age, in a landmark ruling. The decision has cleared the way for dismissed executives to gain compensation, suggesting companies must apply the same standards of procedural fairness for executives as for award employees. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Failed Perth entrepreneur Alan Bond will face up to 10 years jail after yesterday admitting to two counts of acting with intent to defraud Freehold Pty Ltd, a subsidiary of Bell Resources of which he was a director. Bond pleaded guilty under a deal with he Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions which saw five other charges against him dropped. Page 1.

The chances of the Federal Government passing its Telstra legislation through the Senate increased yesterday as the Senate passed the sweeping changes to the Higher Education Contribution Scheme that include the introduction of different charges for degrees and a lower income threshold for paying them. Page 1.

A raid on a Melbourne gem store yesterday left two men dead and a woman with injuries so severe paramedics at the scene were amazed she was still alive. As the woman fought for her life after undergoing emergency surgery, a man was charged over the incident late last night. Page 1.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello yesterday predicted a further boost in Australia's already "solid" economic growth, following the release of national income and expenditure accounts figures showing a 3.8 per cent growth in the year to September 30. Page1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello says Australia's economy is growing slowly, citing the rollout of controversial pay-TV cables as evidence of this growth. His comments came on the release of the National Accounts which showed a 0.8 per cent growth in the economy in the September quarter, and as the Australian dollar dipped down 2.5 cents to around US78.5 cents within the turmoil of global foreign exchange markets. Page 1.

Former America's Cup hero and failed entrepreneur Alan Bond looks likely to spend the remainder of the century in prison after yesterday's surprise admission of guilt on two charges involving a A$700 million loan to the Bond Corporation in 1988 by Freehold which then blew out to A$1 billion. The loans were part of a deal designed to keep Bond Corporation afloat when it was hit with huge debt. Page 1.

A proposal now being negotiated by Stadium Australia, the New South Wales Government and the Sydney Olympic Organising Committee (SOCOG) may see many of the best seats at the 2000 Games sold to companies rather than individuals, following the shortfall in the sale of the Olympic stadium by underwriters of 34,4000 gold memberships at A$10,000 each. Page 1.

A rift has erupted between Independent Commission Against Corruption head Barry O'Keefe QC and some of his staff following an ICAC employee's appearance in the New South Wales Industrial Commission claiming corrupt and unfair practices. O'Keefe made commnts to a mass meeting of ICAC staff on the day of the employee's appearance that have angered the New South Wales Public Service Association. Page 3.
THE AGE

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett has scrapped the A$80 million renovation plans for Parliament House in Melbourne, citing the Opposition's lack of support in allowing sandstone mining in the Grampians national park as the reason. Opposition Leader John Bruby has deemed Kennett's decision as bizarre and irrational. Page A1.

Late last night Manuel Adajian was charged with the murders of a father and son during a bungled armed robbery of their gem merchant's offices. The owner's wife was also shot and is in a critical condition at the Alfred Hospital. Page A1.

Interest rate speculation has seen a spectacular sell-off of the Australian dollar causing a drop of almost three US cents from a six-year high, with trading in the dollar appearing to stabilise on world markets last night. Its partial recovery followed the Reserve Bank's failure to cut interest rates. Page A1.

Symbolic links with the Queen would still be maintained under the Howard Government's compromise plan for a republic, while allowing full constitutional powers to be vested in the Australian head of State and involving minimal constitutional changes. The plan has been put forward in the hope it will satisfy both constitutional monarchists and republicans. Page A1.
